key_facts: Japan's economy unexpectedly contracted in Q3, shrinking at an annualized 0.1% vs the previous quarter, as slower consumption and exports pressured growth.

key_facts: Fraudsters exploit the Black Friday period and the late-January tax return deadline by sending emails, texts and calls impersonating retailers and HMRC, directing victims to fake websites to steal personal information.
HMRC received 95,340 reports of suspected scams in the year to the end of October; 900 reports concerned one scam using emails with a malicious attachment leading to a fake gov.uk page.

HMRC states it never contacts people by email, text or phone to offer a refund or ask them to claim one, never asks for personal or financial information by email or text, and never leaves threatening voicemails about legal action or arrest.

Barclays advises pausing before buying, paying by credit or debit card via a trusted payment service rather than a bank transfer to a stranger, opening official websites or apps directly rather than via links, and contacting the bank immediately if scammed.
importance_reason: Consumer fraud-awareness piece with no direct market-moving event.

key_facts: Gas has begun flowing from the Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea, 150 miles east of Aberdeen, operated by Adura under a Shell/Equinor joint venture; the UK government approved production last month after years of uncertainty and a court case.

Adura says Jackdaw will provide about 6% of UK gas production, enough to power 1.4 million homes, or about 2% of total UK demand after imports; the UK government says it will add £2.9bn to the economy over an expected 11-year lifespan and protect hundreds of jobs.

The decision on Rosebank, the UK's largest known untapped oil field off Shetland, is still pending; Jackdaw and Rosebank consents were struck down by Scottish courts in January 2025 after a challenge by environmental campaigners, following a Supreme Court ruling on climate impact of burning fossil fuels.
Critics including the Scottish Greens ("climate vandalism"), Greenpeace and Oxfam oppose the approval, while Conservatives urged approval of Rosebank too.
importance_reason: Plausible regional energy-supply event with limited scale (~2% of UK demand) and a clear policy angle, but no market-moving shock or systemic impact.
market_link: Restarted domestic North Sea gas supply may marginally reduce UK reliance on imported higher-emission gas and slightly ease winter supply pressure on UK gas prices; a Rosebank decision could add to medium-term North Sea oil supply expectations.

key_facts: The New York fall auction season for modern and contemporary art begins Monday with a combined forecast of $2.8 billion across the three major auction houses.

Sotheby's auction of a van Gogh painting of blossoming chestnut trees, expected to sell for about $180 million, was challenged late by heirs of its Jewish former owner, who claim it was sold under Nazi-era duress in 1936.
The three houses estimate about $600 million more in sales than last November, when a Klimt portrait sold for over $236 million, the second-most expensive painting ever auctioned.
Experts attribute the higher estimates to a surge in high-value works and confidence in ultrawealthy buyers despite possible rising interest rates and recent stock market volatility.

key_facts: A planned American-led artificial intelligence hub in the Philippines has sparked opposition over concerns about displacement, resources and national sovereignty.

In May, Capas mayor Roseller Rodriguez learned from news reports, not an official invitation, that American officials had arrived in his district to start an AI hub; he had never heard about the hub beforehand.

The initiative is called Pax Silica; it was launched by the United States last December to unite partners around AI supply chains independent of China and is part of President Trump's effort to counter Beijing's economic and technological influence.

Trump administration officials describe Pax Silica as a 21st-century successor to 'Pax Americana'. Open questions raised locally include water and electricity sources and the fate of farmers living on the site; the article states Rodriguez has few answers months later.

The 2009 government standard contract template caps agreements at seven years and includes protections for artists' well-being and trademark rights after the terms end; it remains largely legally nonbinding, and a government survey found some companies do not use it at all.
NewJeans' contracts run until 2029; a court held the members to them after they attempted to quit their label two years ago.
